sources.title: RIT CSCI-636 Information Retrieval catalog description
sources.author: Rochester Institute of Technology
sources.content: An introduction to the theories and techniques used to construct search engines. Topics include search interfaces, traditional retrieval models (e.g., TF-IDF, BM25), modern retrieval techniques (e.g., neural reranking and retrieval), search engine evaluation, and search applications (e.g., conversational IR, enterprise search). Students will also review current IR research, provide written summaries of current research papers, and complete a group project in which they will design and execute experiments for search engine components. Prerequisites:(CSCI-603 and CSCI-605 and CSCI-661 with grades of B or better, including familiarity with computer science concepts) or CSCI-331 or equivalent courses. Students may not take and receive credit for both CSCI-636 and CSCI-536. Contact Hours: Lecture 3 Typically Offered: Spring

sources.title: scikit-learn User Guide
sources.author: scikit-learn developers
sources.content: Data-analysis workflows separate data preparation, exploratory analysis, training, validation, testing, model selection, and evaluation. Supervised methods learn mappings from examples paired with target labels, while unsupervised methods identify structure without targets. Preprocessing must be fitted only on permitted training data to avoid leakage. Pipelines combine transformations and estimators so the same operations are applied consistently. Cross-validation repeats training and validation across defined splits. Grouping, dimensionality reduction, classification, regression, and clustering answer different questions and require appropriate assumptions and metrics. Evaluation must match the task and the cost of errors, while distribution shift, missing data, overfitting, and unexamined sampling choices can invalidate conclusions.

sources.title: PostgreSQL Documentation
sources.author: PostgreSQL Global Development Group
sources.content: Data systems organize records with declared types, tables, rows, columns, keys, and constraints. Queries select, join, aggregate, order, and transform data. Indexes provide additional access paths for selected workloads. Transactions group operations and isolation controls how concurrent operations observe one another. Query planning and physical storage affect performance without changing logical query meaning. Analytical work should preserve provenance from captured data through cleaning, transformation, grouping, modeling, visualization, and reporting. Data quality analysis makes missingness, duplicates, inconsistent representation, integrity constraints, sampling, and update behavior explicit.
